name: Vera Rios
life: Vera built her fortune keeping food cold for businesses that couldn't buy their own storage. During the first summer she slept beside a faulty alarm. Today plenty of people call her generous. Very few remember that she used to owe the snack seller lunch money. Friday often includes a stop at Harbour Bakery, where Vera buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: For years I bought my crews soup from that cart. I gave the big check because I wanted my late wife's name on a bench. Now the vendor is asking who can actually afford to sit there at lunchtime.
appearance: Vera has a long silver braid, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a dark green knitted vest. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Vera turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Vera admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Vera learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To put a memorial where her wife would actually have spent a lunch break.
family: Emma Davis is Vera’s second cousin. Vera picks the meeting place. Emma sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A room above the dryers*, Emma says, “I live across the landing. I asked for free sittings for the old people nobody photographs unless they're blowing candles out.”
connections: Gil Atwood (former lunch vendor). They knew each other over a cart long before anybody put their names on the same check.
